marks.gloss_en: כי הא -- running through the gemara first and analysing afterwards illustrates the migras/iyun distinction (kind svara: the corpus convention for כי הא ד-)
as when (Rava and Rami) bar Chama stood before Rav Chisda: they ran through the gemara together, and then analysed the reasoning (names textually uncertain -- header)
Rava: drinking vessels -- in the sukkah
תא שמע: עד שיאור ויעלה עמוד השחר -- read with alef that is said twice (תרתי?!), so אלא אימא: עד שיעור ויעלה עמוד השחר
the cited baraita: [he is not troubled to go up] until שיאור and the dawn rises
אמר ליה אביי: והא תנן משתסרח המקפה! -- splinters do not spoil the porridge, so leaving is not yet permitted
לדידי, כיון דאנינא דעתאי, כמי שתסרח המקפה דמי לי -- for a delicate person this already counts as the spoiling (= p_anina_daatai)
the wind blew and brought splinters; Rav Yosef said: clear my vessels from here
if he was eating in the sukkah, rain fell and he went down, he is not troubled to go up until he finishes his meal
when the sun is eclipsed it is a bad sign for the whole world
R' Meir: whenever the lights are eclipsed it is a bad sign for the enemies of Israel
when the sun is eclipsed it is a bad sign for the nations
its face resembles blood -- the sword comes to the world
there is no nation that is smitten whose god is not smitten with it
for four things the sun is eclipsed: for a head of the court who died and is not eulogised properly
and for four things the lights are eclipsed: for writers of forged documents
and for four things householders' property is handed to the kingdom: for those who keep paid-up bonds
תא שמע דתניא: שפך לו רבו קיתון על פניו ואמר לו אי אפשי בשמושך -- the baraita says outright that the master poured
his master poured a jug in his face and said to him: I do not want your service
it was taught: from when a mikpa of grisin (pounded grain) would spoil -- specifying the mishnah's mikpa
